title: Death Race
full_review:
"Death Race" (Universal/Relativity) is a brooding, dystopian futuristic action tale about speedway gladiators forced into mortal competition for public entertainment.

One such competitor is former factory laborer Jensen Ames (Jason Statham). Framed for the murder of his wife, he's consigned to an island prison overseen by icy, manipulative Warden Hennessey (Joan Allen). She offers him his freedom if he competes in the titular three-day ordeal, which is transmitted live to millions of subscribers over the Internet, and which she supervises on behalf of the jail's for-profit owners.

Anxious to be reunited with his infant daughter, Ames agrees. He's given the assistance of a female convict navigator (Natalie Martinez) and a skilled pit crew (Ian McShane, Fred Koehler and Jacob Vargas), and sets out to eliminate -- all too literally -- the competition.

Writer-director Paul W.S. Anderson's updating of Paul Bartel's 1975 "Death Race 2000" is one long paean to brutality, as characters are decapitated, gored and napalmed.

The film contains pervasive graphic violence with blood, fleeting rear nudity, frequent rough and crude language, and a couple of profanities. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
